INTRO: ^He closes the book, though he leaves one finger between the pages.

c-3: ^You move away from the desk and return to the centre of the room.
^The Keeper opens up his book again and continues writing.

WHO: ^The Keeper smiles softly and studies you for a moment. His brown eyes stare into your own and you feel as though in a trance, before he blinks and the feeling is gone. "That depends on what you mean."
^"No," he says. "It isn't." He looks down at the book beneath his hand. "But names are useful things. They tell you where someone belongs. What they were called. Sometimes what they became."
^You don't appreciate the Keeper's skillful evasion of your question. "So what were you called?" you press.
^There is silence for an uncomfortably long time.
^"What? You don't remember your own name?"

^"I remember many things that happened to me. I remember rooms I haven't seen in years. I remember the last words of people who have been dead for longer than you've been alive." He turns a page. "But my own name is gone."
^"That's the trouble with memory. You don't always notice something disappearing until it's gone."
HOW: ^"Hah," the Keeper smirks. "Ossaneth doesn't send people in here without lessing us know somethings, at least."
ASK: ^"The Ossuary?" He glances past you at seemingly nothing. "It is a place for the dead."
DEAD: ^"No." The Keeper fixes his eyes back on you. "But that would be simpler."
BUILT: ^"I don't know. Ossaneth, maybe. Something else, maybe. All I know is what the records say."
^I know which stones are older than others. I know where the walls have been repaired. I know which names appear in the oldest records.”
^“But whoever built the first part of this place left very little behind.”
